title: Turning Debt
designBriefSource: The requested six-family planning batch; private prompt retained outside distribution.
stageDependency: Align the shield -> use the upper clear bay -> preserve the far turning input -> return to the lower junction -> ascend through an earlier lane using the same shield -> leave at the northern doorway.
planningBurden: A previously crossed gate becomes an obstacle again. Overshooting a useful bay loses the only way to change pushing side.
changedConstraints: The final route crosses an earlier shield lane instead of following the source rectangle.
Staggered clear bays create specific future input obligations.
A stopping wall closes an experimentally found direct northward bypass.
physicalScope: One 16 by 16 room; ordinary pinned official engine; all initial actors at elevation zero.

difficulty.qualification: An author estimate from dependent operations and planning tradeoffs, not calibrated human difficulty.

limits: The tested turning inputs and north-south-north reuse are necessary for this fixed doorway goal.
No unique shortest solution or necessity of every individual floor cell is claimed.
